title: Pea protein
description: Lead, cadmium, mercury and arsenic evidence for pea protein isolate and concentrate: four independently tested products, manufacturer batch data submitted to FDA, applicable limits and what a buyer should ask a supplier.
lede: Four independently tested pea protein products and 15 manufacturer batch results carry the published metal evidence for pea protein: cadmium was found in most results, lead at low levels, and inorganic arsenic has never been measured.

answers.text: Cadmium and lead are the supported concerns: both were quantified in two independently tested retail powders and in most manufacturer batches. Inorganic arsenic is unmeasured, and total arsenic appears only as manufacturer results below their reporting limits.

citation_spans.after: Cadmium and lead are the supported concerns: both were quantified in two independently tested retail powders and in most manufacturer batches.
Inorganic arsenic is unmeasured, and total arsenic appears only as manufacturer results below their reporting limits.

answers.text: Lot testing for inorganic arsenic, lead and cadmium deserves priority, because two retail powders differed more than twofold in cadmium at nearly equal lead. Origin-based sourcing cannot be prioritized on current evidence.

citation_spans.after: Lot testing for inorganic arsenic, lead and cadmium deserves priority, because two retail powders differed more than twofold in cadmium at nearly equal lead.

passages.question: What does "not detected" mean on a pea protein certificate?
